citation: Afonso P., Forte P., Branquinho L., Ferraz R., Garrido N.D., Teixeira J.E. (2025). Shaping Training Load, Technical-Tactical Behaviour, and Well-Being in Football: A Systematic Review. Sports 13(8):244. doi:10.3390/sports13080244
design_method: Systematic review (PubMed, Scopus, WoS); 341 records screened, 46 studies, 1,763 players aged ~13-29
key_findings: Mostly physical external load (GPS) and internal load (sRPE, HR); 22 studies tracked well-being; only 5 used multivariate models; monitoring is fragmented
limitations: Heterogeneous studies; calls for standardised multidimensional frameworks, esp. youth and sub-elite
relevance_to_project: Justifies a multidimensional model (load + wellness + performance) for youth players

citation: Authors to be added (see publisher page). (2026). A call for consensus: a narrative review of GPS-based external training load monitoring in male youth soccer players. Sports 14(4):152.
key_findings: Common variables: total distance, high-speed running, sprint distance, distance/min, peak speed, acc/dec counts; position, drill format and season phase affect demands
limitations: Speed thresholds, acceleration definitions and processing differ between studies, hindering comparison
relevance_to_project: Our KPI catalogue must fix explicit, documented definitions and thresholds; keep them configurable

citation: Tang Q., Wei X., Tan B. (2026). The Role of Machine Learning in Talent Identification for Team Sports: A Systematic Review. J Sports Sci Med 25(1):58-83. doi:10.52082/jssm.2026.58
design_method: Systematic review; 228 records, 27 studies, youth team sports (mostly soccer)
key_findings: Random forest and gradient boosting most common; discrimination modest to excellent; calibration rarely assessed; external validation uncommon; 59% high risk of bias
limitations: ML should complement, not replace, traditional methods; small/biased datasets
relevance_to_project: Supports a transparent rule-based core with ML only as an evaluated extension

citation: Teixeira J.E., Alves A.R., Ferraz R., Forte P., Leal M., Ribeiro J., Silva A.J., Barbosa T.M., Monteiro A.M. (2022). Effects of Chronological Age, Relative Age, and Maturation Status on Accumulated Training Load and Perceived Exertion in Young Sub-Elite Football Players. Front Physiol 13:832202. doi:10.3389/fphys.2022.832202
design_method: Observational, 60 male sub-elite academy players, 6 weeks, GPS + HR + RPE
key_findings: Age, relative age and maturity band were linked to differences in accumulated load (e.g. acceleration/deceleration counts); perceived exertion differed little
limitations: Single academy, small sample, short period
relevance_to_project: Maturity/relative age must be stored and used when interpreting load and test results

citation: Ribeiro N., Gonzalo-Skok O., Valente-Dos-Santos J., Mandorino M., Beato M., Salter J., Nobari H., Loureiro N., Ferreira R., Araujo J.P., Tavares F. (2026). Impact of biological maturation on match workload in Portuguese elite male academy soccer players. Biol Sport 43:1329-1340. doi:10.5114/biolsport.2026.161102
design_method: Longitudinal, 60 elite male U14-U17 players, six time points over two seasons; maturity from % predicted adult height
key_findings: Chronological age predicted high-speed running and sprint distance per minute; total distance and acc/dec per minute depended on age x maturity interaction, strongest in younger players
relevance_to_project: Use age AND maturity status (% predicted adult height) as context for KPI norms

citation: Majumdar A., Bakirov R., Hodges D., Scott S., Rees T. (2022). Machine Learning for Understanding and Predicting Injuries in Football. Sports Med Open 8:73. (PMC9174408)
design_method: Review of ML use on training/competition load and injury
key_findings: ML can clarify the load-injury relationship
limitations: Variables used as load proxies vary; data-imbalance handling differs; few multi-season datasets
relevance_to_project: Injury prediction is out of scope; warns about data scarcity and imbalance for ML

citation: Felfernig A., Wundara M., Tran T.N.T., Le V.-M., Lubos S., Polat-Erdeniz S. (2024). Sports Recommender Systems: Overview and Research Issues. J Intell Inf Syst. doi:10.1007/s10844-024-00857-w (arXiv:2312.03785)
key_findings: Covers training, tactics, injury prevention, nutrition; knowledge-based, content-based, collaborative, hybrid approaches; open issues incl. explanations, evaluation metrics, psychological aspects
limitations: Few evaluated systems; evaluation metrics immature
relevance_to_project: Knowledge-based recommendation + explanations fits our scarce-data setting; defines research issues to address

citation: An P. (2024). Fuzzy Decision Support Systems to Improve the Effectiveness of Training Programs in the Field of Sports Fitness. Int J Comput Intell Syst 17:168. doi:10.1007/s44196-024-00555-z
design_method: Fuzzy (Mamdani) decision system on the PMData dataset (16 participants, 5 months)
key_findings: Proposed FMDS reported to outperform FAHP, F-RBF and EDM on several indices
limitations: Comparison mainly qualitative; tiny dataset; not youth football
relevance_to_project: Shows rule/fuzzy-based decision support for training is publishable; also shows evaluation weakness we must avoid

citation: Jauhiainen S., Ayramo S., Forsman H., Kauppi J.-P. (2019). Talent identification in soccer using a one-class support vector machine. Int J Comput Sci Sport 18(3):125-136. doi:10.2478/ijcss-2019-0021
key_findings: Mean AUC-ROC 0.763; physical tests were most informative
relevance_to_project: Evidence that simple physical field tests carry predictive information for youth players

citation: Impellizzeri F.M., Marcora S.M., Coutts A.J. (2019). Internal and External Training Load: 15 Years On. Int J Sports Physiol Perform 14(2):270-273. doi:10.1123/ijspp.2018-0935
key_findings: Defines internal vs external training load and clarifies the framework
relevance_to_project: Our data model separates external and internal load

citation: Gabbett T.J. (2016). The training-injury prevention paradox: should athletes be training smarter and harder? Br J Sports Med 50(5):273-280
key_findings: Rapid load increases linked to non-contact injuries; acute:chronic workload ratio proposed as a monitoring tool
limitations: Conceptual; ACWR thresholds need local validation
relevance_to_project: Basis for load-spike rules (thresholds configurable and validated with coaches)

citation: Rossi A., Pappalardo L., Cintia P., Iaia F.M., Fernandez J., Medina D. (2018). Effective injury forecasting in soccer with GPS training data and machine learning. PLoS ONE 13(7):e0201264. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0201264
design_method: ML forecaster trained on GPS data from one professional season
key_findings: Reports accurate and interpretable injury forecasting; aims at practical rules
relevance_to_project: Shows value of interpretable rules; also shows dependence on GPS hardware we do not assume

citation: Nikolaidis P.T., Clemente F.M., van der Linden C.M.I., Rosemann T., Knechtle B. (2018). Validity and Reliability of 10-Hz Global Positioning System to Assess In-line Movement and Change of Direction. Front Physiol 9:228. doi:10.3389/fphys.2018.00228
key_findings: Good validity/reliability for linear movement; lower accuracy for short distances with direction changes
relevance_to_project: Data-quality caveat for any imported GPS data; justifies data-quality flags

key_findings: Digital Football Hub, youth pathway, 1.5 million participants target
limitations: Strategy summary, not a technical spec
